sections.h2: Which Warren offices set and collect your property tax?
sections.html:
Two city offices split the work. The Assessing Department builds the roll and keeps data on 59,077 parcels, about 54,620 of them real property. The Treasurer's Office sends the bills and collects for every taxing unit inside the city, which includes the city itself, six school districts and the county.

Warren sits in Macomb County, so the Macomb County Treasurer takes over any bill that is still unpaid after the city's collection period ends. The Assessing Department's page offers free BS&A lookups of ownership, values and tax history by owner name, address or parcel number, which is the quickest way to see what is owed before you list.

Bills go out twice a year, in the first week of July and the first week of December. The city states that not receiving a bill does not excuse the payment, so call the Treasurer's Office at 586-574-4542 if a copy never arrives.

sections.h2: When are Warren property taxes due, and what do late payments cost?
sections.html:
Summer taxes carry the city and school levies, and winter taxes carry the county's. Warren allows the summer bill in two parts, which the city's own overview calls rare among Michigan cities. The first installment runs about 62 percent of the summer total.

Warren tax calendar and late charges from the city Treasurer's pages
BillPayableAfter that
Summer, full amount or first installmentJuly 1 to August 31From September 1 only the full summer tax is accepted, with 1% in September and one half of 1% for each later month
Summer, second installmentBilled December 1, due by January 31From February 1 a 3.5% fee applies to unpaid summer tax
Winter (county)December 1 to February 28Unpaid balances go to the Macomb County Treasurer with the city's fees

A check counts only after it clears, and a postmark on or before the due date protects you from penalties. Fiscal years differ by levy: city and schools run July 1 to June 30, the county runs January 1 to December 31, and the state education tax runs October 1 to September 30.

sections.h2: What happens to a Warren tax bill left unpaid after February?
sections.html:
It becomes delinquent and is payable only to the Macomb County Treasurer. The city's payment page says the county adds all the city's collection fees plus another 4 percent fee and 1 percent interest for each month until the bill is paid.

The city's tax town hall overview adds that the Warren Treasurer cannot legally collect after that point, and that the county offers payment plans and other help to people trying to stay in their homes. Its advice is to call early instead of waiting for foreclosure steps to begin.

For a seller, an open county balance is the item that most often delays a closing, since the title company must see it paid. Pull the parcel's BS&A record two or three weeks before you sign a purchase agreement so the figure is not a surprise.

sections.h2: Can a Warren homeowner delay the summer tax bill?
sections.html:
Some can. The Treasurer's Office offers a deferment that pushes the summer due date to February 14, if the household meets every one of these tests:

  • Yearly household income of $40,000 or less.
  • The property is the owner's primary residence.
  • The owner is 62 or older, or is an eligible veteran, serviceperson, widow or widower, a blind person, or someone totally and permanently disabled or paraplegic, hemiplegic or quadriplegic.

Forms are mailed each July to people who filed the year before. New applicants call the Treasurer's Office at 586-574-4554 starting in July. The completed form is due by September 15.

Other relief runs through the assessor. A poverty exemption for a principal residence is decided by the Board of Review at its March, July or December session and lasts one year. The disabled veteran homestead exemption under MCL 211.7b needs an affidavit filed with the City Assessor by December 30, along with Veterans Affairs documents.

sections.h2: How do you appeal a Warren assessment?
sections.html:
For a house, the only route is the March Board of Review. Residential owners must protest there to keep the right to go on to the Michigan Tax Tribunal for valuation disputes. The five-member board hears complaints from anyone who feels over-assessed and can adjust individual assessments.

In 2026, hearings ran March 11, 16 and 17, with appointments booked through the Assessing Department at 586-574-4532 and written appeals due by 5:00 p.m. on March 17. The appeal had to reach 1 City Square, Suite 310. Appeals cannot be filed by email or online, so use an in-person appointment or a letter. Expect a similar March schedule every year, announced in the city's notice and on your assessment change notice sent each February.

  • Put your name, address, phone number, parcel number and reasons in a written appeal, and sign it.
  • Bring sales data or an appraisal, because the owner carries the burden of proving true cash value.
  • Send an agent only with a signed authorization letter.
  • Expect decisions by mail after the board adjourns, not at the hearing.

July and December sessions hear poverty exemptions and qualified error corrections, but never opinions of value. Commercial and industrial real property may go straight to the Tax Tribunal by May 31.

sections.h2: How does a sale change the taxable value on a Warren home?
sections.html:
It resets it. Assessed value is half of estimated market value, and taxable value normally rises each year by the lesser of 5 percent or the inflation rate multiplier. When a property changes hands, the taxable value in the following year is set equal to the assessed value, which the city calls uncapping.

The city's assessing overview shows how large the swing can be: owners who held for years can pay a much smaller bill than the buyer who follows them. The buyer's bill depends on the millage rates of whichever of Warren's six school districts serves the address, which is why the state's property tax estimator is worth running before you advertise a price.

A principal residence exemption lowers the school operating millage for an owner who lives in the home. Sellers should tell buyers the exemption ends with the sale, and buyers who will live there must file for it themselves.

sections.h2: What do title companies need from Warren sellers?
sections.html:
Three items come up repeatedly. First, MCL 211.135 requires proof that taxes were paid for the five years before a warranty deed, and the county treasurer issues the certificate. A quitclaim deed with no warranty covenants does not need it.

Second, the Warren Treasurer's Office asks mortgage and title companies to include the tax bill with its scannable barcode. Without a bill, a $2.00 duplicate bill fee applies, and it rises to $5.00 per parcel if the city has to chase the missing bill.

Third, the payment itself. Warren takes online payments through a portal that charges nothing for bank account payments and 2.8 percent, with a $1.50 minimum, for cards. It also accepts payment by phone at 1-844-435-3977, by mail, at City Hall and through secure drop boxes behind the Civic Center Library and the Maybelle Burnette Library.

sections.h2: What is Warren like for someone selling a house?
sections.html:
Warren is the largest community in Macomb County and the third-largest city in Michigan, covering about 34 square miles between 8 Mile and 14 Mile roads on the Detroit border. The city incorporated on January 1, 1957, and grew around the General Motors Technical Center, the Detroit Arsenal and the Chrysler truck plant. Center Line is a small city fully enclosed by Warren. I-696 crosses it east to west, Van Dyke is M-53, and Mound Road is a main north-south artery.

The Census Bureau estimates 137,138 residents for 2025 and counts 54,744 households. Owners occupy 71.1 percent of homes, the median owner-occupied value is $193,400, median household income is $64,016 and median gross rent is $1,225. Density is about 4,055 people per square mile. A parcel's own assessment and millage, not these averages, decide its bill.

faqs.q: When is the first summer property tax installment due in Warren?
faqs.a: By August 31. The summer bill can be paid in full or in two parts, with the second installment billed December 1 and due by January 31. From September 1 only the full summer tax is accepted, with a 1 percent fee in September and one half of 1 percent monthly afterward.

faqs.q: Where do I pay Warren winter taxes after February 28?
faqs.a: To the Macomb County Treasurer. After the last day of February the city can no longer take the payment, and the county adds the city's fees plus a 4 percent fee and 1 percent interest per month.

faqs.q: Can I appeal my Warren assessment online?
faqs.a: No. Warren accepts appeals only in person by appointment or by letter received before the deadline, and residential owners must use the March Board of Review before going to the Michigan Tax Tribunal.

faqs.q: Does a Warren property tax bill change when I sell?
faqs.a: Yes, for the buyer. The year after a sale the taxable value is set equal to the assessed value, which is half of market value. That can raise the bill well above what the seller paid under the capped value.

faqs.q: Who can defer Warren summer taxes?
faqs.a: Primary-residence owners with household income of $40,000 or less who are 62 or older or fit a listed veteran, widow, blind or disabled category. The form is due by September 15 and extends the summer due date to February 14.
